Unlike most of the hell's denizens, Changelings are alive, not demons. [PARAGRAPH]Occasionally Changelings are sent into the mortal world of Erebus to perform tasks for Esus. They often sire children (most commonly by replacing a lover) with mortal women. The orthodox opinion of every religion or mage guild in Erebus holds that only rare individuals are blessed (or, in some cases, cursed) with affinity for any sort of magic. It is sacrilige to suggest that every mortal soul shares a natural gift in every precept, but this heresy happens to be true. While most men's affinities are too weak to be of much use, there are ways to awaken them. The architects of the Tower of Mastery go to great lengths to talk around this point rather than state it directly, but their ambition is let every mage match the powers of Kylorin.

[ICON_BULLET]Cannot fall in an [LINK=SPELL_ARENA_BATTLE]Arena battle[\\LINK][NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Being an Aspect of War is the highest blessing Camulos can grant, but he does not care who gets it so long as they use their power to kill. It is given at birth and cannot be revoked. All the Aspects have superhuman martial prowess, both in personal strength and in tactics. While they may not defeat whole armies on their own, in single combat are nearly invincible. Some are Good, some are Evil, and some are hostile towards both extremes, but they cannot remain neutral in any conflict for long. They are the cause of most wars, regardless of their intent. Notable Aspects of War include Arak the Erkling, Capria, Mahon the Butcher, Orthus, Magnadine, Surder, and Makhai. [NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET]Every god created seven Aspects, True Angels whose inherent affinity is exceeded only by that of the archangels or the gods themselves, and whose freedom to act in creation is not limited by The Compact. The original Aspects of War were vanquished early int he Godswar, but whenever one falls it is reincarnated as a mortal. Years can pass before an Aspect of War is reborn, but there are usually 5 to 7 active in the world at any time. The Sons of Discord try to track them individuals down and use them to cause more conflict.

Recruits 6 Hill Giants to the player's cause.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]Early explorers found it was best to avoid the massive giants that roamed the land. A bard, named Antonis of Oriel, wandered too close and was captured by a group called the Nilhorn. He offered the only gift he could for his life, he played a song. The wild giants were so entranced by his song that, when it ended, they sat unmoving and Antonis could have simply walked out of the makeshift camp they had dragged him back to. Fascinated by finding his new audience so appreciative, Antonis continued to play, and his performances became a part of the giants' nightly rituals.[PARAGRAPH:1]Antonis stayed with the Nilhorn for three years, until one of them reported seeing a Sheaim army approaching his homeland. The giants avoided any settled land and tried to convince Antonis not to return, but he left the giants and returned to defend Oriel. Although a talented musician, Antonis was an incompetent warrior and he was killed defending Oriel. When he fell, the Nilhorn came out of the forests and approached the besieged village. Both armies froze, unaccustomed to seeing giants willing to enter civilized lands. Searching the battlefield, the giants found Antonis's body, and, enraged, they set upon the Sheaim. The village defenders cheered at their new-found allies and joined in the assault.[PARAGRAPH:1]The battle was quick and the Sheaim were turned back. After it was over, the giants picked up the body of Antonis and carried it with them into the forests. The village raised a monument to their large rescuers and swore never to forget the aid they were given. The Sheaim never forgot the failed battle either, and forever avoided Oriel in their attacks.

There have always been men that ran toward danger. In the age of Magic, some were known as the Brotherhood of Wardens. They were a secret organization that tried to protect the citizens of Patria from cruel edicts of the Imprimator Council. They rescued elven captives from the Duchy of Dust, chattel slaves from Candlefast, and debtors from the Duchy of Glimmerhome. [PARAGRAPH]The organization started as a secular one, but the archangel Pelian the Suffering was inspired by the brave members of the brotherhood. When the rebellions began and the war started between the Empyrean, the Sanctus Inquisition and the Imprimatur Council, the Brotherhood attempted to make sure that the weak and innocent weren't destroyed in that war. [PARAGRAPH]They had middling success. Many were lost. But if they could get those they rescued back to the Duchy of Logos, they would find the tides would turn in their favor. Enemies spells were weakened, rotting wolves would lose their scent, their own endurance, and hope returned. This was the arda of Sirona and the blessing she offered for their cause. "[PARAGRAPH:2]The Brotherhood of Wardens is a cult of Sirona that teaches men that they must do whatever they can to protect the least among them. The orthodox Wardens were exterminated in Calabim lands, but Alexis encourages the spread of a heretical sect that believes the best way to protect the meek is to teach them to passively accept any form of oppression without every trying to fight back. [PARAGRAPH:2]Pelian disobeyed Sirona during the Godswar. Sirona commanded that compassion required the defense of creation, but Pelian refused to be violent and abandoned her army. After suffering a massive defeat Sirona lay nearly destroyed. As the army of Aeron closed in, Pelian returned and placed a sanctuary around Sirona. Pelian was attacked, but he still refused to fight. Instead he was torn and tortured for 21 days and bore the worst of Aeron's torments. His body is forever broken from this ordeal. But after 21 days Sirona was revived and came out of the sanctuary to rescue her archangel and scatter the army of Aeron. The breaking of the compassionate Pelian was an example to the gods that the compact was needed. [PARAGRAPH]Pelian lay recovering for centuries. It wasn't until the Age of Ice that he gazed again into creation, drawn by the calls of those suffering. There was little he could directly do, but he whispered to the great Eurabatres, who was sleeping nearby and awoke the dragon, calling him to aid those in need. [PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Rebirth he attempted to calm the heart of Basium, before he marched through into hell. Pelian warned that his hubris would lead him into serving Agares, or at least remove his blessed protection from creation. But Basium ignored him and marched through the Throne of Hell. Pelian wept for him and those doomed to be lost with him. [PARAGRAPH]During the Age of Invention, when the Matronae came for the worshipers of the old gods, Pelian's spirit was with the few remaining worshipers of Sirona and called for them to be non-violent. He called for calm as they stood before the Shrine of Sirona, as their statues were torn down, as their holy texts were burned and as each worshiper of Sirona that refused to forsake their goddess was executed. Then he gathered their souls and carried them to the Isle of Birds. The Stewards of Inequity are a cult to Mammon, although few of their members will ever realize this. Mammon prefers his follows believe that they serve only their own self interest. The Stewards hate any sort of honest work but will go to great lengths to amass fortunes. Most are already very wealthy and powerful men when they join this cult, although some are merely covetous and believe membership will help further their ambitions. Its ranks include many tax collectors, regulators, government lobbyists, almost every central banker, the upper management in most large companies, and even many priests high in the hierarchies of other faiths. Few Stewards rank high enough to ever learn of the existence of the cabal that convenes to decide the policies they all execute. Most are just happy to play their small part towards the lofty goal of making the rick richer and the poor poorer.
